name: meld
invariant: Meld is structural composition (the free monoidal tensor) of two independently-generated histories -- concatenation of event logs -- and is distinct from Bind-based concurrency, which couples elements within a single shared history instead of combining two separate ones.
explanation: Meld operates directly on two History values before either is under a single Arbiter's option-space accounting, so it does not fit the single-Arbiter event-stream schema the other fixtures use here. Instead of a single `initial_option_space`/`events`/`expect` block, this fixture provides two independent `history_a`/`history_b` sub-histories (each with its own Ω and event sequence, validated and executed through its own Arbiter); a conforming runner then melds the two resulting histories -- by concatenating their event logs, matching `spherepop-kernel::History::meld` (spherepop-kernel/src/history.rs) -- and checks the combined length against `expect_melded_history_len`. This is executed end-to-end by all three runners (Rust, Python, C).
